result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_id_from_label()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the integer ID for a node by its label. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4666-L4711){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_id_from_label(label) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Id from label](/assets/graphs/get-id-from-label.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph with node ids in pills. The queried label C is outlined in the accent color and its id pill, 3, is highlighted. The card returns 3." width="100%"} Translates a human-readable string label to the internal `u64` node ID. Useful when you need the ID for operations that require integer identifiers. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The string label to look up. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The u64 node ID if found, or `None` if the label doesn't exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Node IDs are auto-assigned starting at `1`, so the first node added gets ID `1`: ::: {#8441c506 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") ) graph.get_id_from_label("Alice") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: An unknown label returns `None` rather than raising an error: ::: {#8baf87ec .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_id_from_label("Unknown") ``` :::
